warmup.text: Chapter 18 is the hardest chapter in the book. It is the chapter Isaac told you about on the first page. Read it slowly. If it feels heavy, that is all right. Today you will reread one passage and trace an idea back to where you first met it.

words.text: Put the sight roots to work today. Then the sound alike words again, sorted a new way: is the word a thing, an action, or two words squeezed? Say it in a sentence to check. Then five new words in the spyglass.

reading.text: Read Chapter 18 in your book. Isaac says good-bye to his mother, and then the chapter changes everything. Notice the words from his father that Isaac remembers. Then try the Read Like a Writer box, and finish with the Virtue Watch.

assignment.text: Three questions about Chapter 18. The last one looks back across Chapters 16, 17 and 18. Then revise with the checklist, and work on your second moment. Choose a comparison that fits the feeling of the moment.

glossary.meaning: a thing in a story that stands for a bigger idea

terrified: A councilwoman says this about Naomi.
stickball: Young ghosts hold a bat for it.
mourning: It turns a sunny day quiet.
suffering: Nani Humma asks if it will ever be over.
courage: Isaac walks to the campfire with it.

miss.affect: To affect is to change or influence. It is an action (a verb).
miss.council: A council is a group of leaders. It names a thing.
miss.accept: To accept is to take what is offered. It is an action (a verb).
miss.effect: An effect is a result. It names a thing (a noun).
miss.it's: It's is two words squeezed: it is. Try saying it is in the sentence.
miss.led: Led is the past of lead: she led the way. It is an action.
miss.principle: A principle is a rule or belief. It names a thing.
miss.they're: They're is two words squeezed: they are.

game.title: The Spyglass
game.sub: This week's word game · 5 words today
game.look: Isaac sees what other people cannot see. In this game, a brass spyglass looks at one word at a time. First tap the root hiding inside it: vis or vid means see, and spect means look. The root lights up. Then tap what the word means. Every word you get adds a star to the spyglass.

do: Look at the word in the spyglass.
Tap the root you find inside it.
Tap what the word means.
Tap Next word.
how.why: If you can spot a root, you can work out a long word you have never seen.

opts: pictures you can see from far away
words.why: Yes. Tele means far. Television lets you see things far away.

opts: to look forward to something happening
words.why: Yes. To expect is to look ahead for something you think will happen.
Yes. On a foggy day, visibility is low.

opts: one side of something you look at
words.why: Yes. An aspect is one side of a thing, the way it looks from one place.

opts: to picture something in your mind
words.why: Yes. To visualize is to see a picture in your head.

art.title: Blue Hole, Little Miami River
art.alt: A painting of a calm pool in a river, surrounded by green trees, with three small figures on the rocks.
art.look: Robert S. Duncanson painted this quiet river in Ohio in 1851. It is far from Isaac's road, but it fits Chapter 18: the snow has melted, the sun shines, and the walkers rest by an old pine near the river.

virtue.name: courage
virtue.title: The courage meter
virtue.intro: Think about one moment from Chapter 18.
virtue.moment: Isaac watches his family grieve. He wants to float back into his body and tell them he is all right. Then he remembers his father's words about the bloody footprints, and he does not go back.
virtue.ask: How much courage did Isaac show? Slide to show.
virtue.take: Mason's take: a lot. Going back would have felt easier. Isaac kept his eyes on where he was going, the way his father taught him in Chapter 10.
